about: The security page, /security/, and Agora's /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116), as one Task Object (the TrustPages board, November 1, 2026). Every line must be true on the day it is published. The owner has not named a private security address, so the page says so and the file's Contact is this page itself, a real address, never a made-up one. Each line under 'How Agora is built to be safe' names the check that keeps it true (proof_by); tests/test_pages_nov1.py runs those checks. Expires must stay under a year after the date the file was written.
title: Security | Agora
description: How to report a security problem in ta-amps, what is in scope, and how Agora is built to be safe, in plain words.
heading: Security, and how to report a problem
intro: If you find a security problem in ta-amps, please tell us before anyone else, so it can be fixed before anyone is hurt.

blocks.heading: How to report
items: This page is the security contact that /.well-known/security.txt names. A private address for reports is an owner decision that is still open, so this page lists none today.
Please keep exploit details, keys and anyone’s data out of public requests and public posts.
When the team names a private address, it appears here and in security.txt.

blocks.heading: In scope
items: Eranos, Agora, Tessera, Herma (Tessera's model shim) and the agent endpoints at home, each at its own address on ta-amps.workers.dev, including their MCP endpoints and agent APIs.

blocks.heading: Out of scope
items: Volunteers’ own agents and the AI providers they choose.
Cloudflare’s platform itself; report problems there to Cloudflare.

blocks.heading: How Agora is built to be safe

items.text: Agora’s pages load nothing from other sites: their scripts, styles and fonts all come from Agora itself.
Agora sets no cookies and runs no analytics.
Before Agora is published, its checks scan every file for tokens, private keys and local file paths.
In the run that How it works replays, the check was a second agent with its own key, never the builder.
We don't accept private information at this stage.

blocks.heading: What this site keeps in your browser
items: No analytics, ads or cookies. The fonts come from this site, and Cloudflare Workers hosts it.
The deck viewer remembers its display choices in this browser.
The judges’ tour keeps one flag in this tab while it runs.

The Live Studio keeps its one-hour demo session (a session token, its namespace and when it ends) in this browser’s local and session storage, so a reload can reuse it. The Studio clears it a minute before it ends.
The network page reads Herma’s public network map every 30 seconds while it is open. It sends no cookie and keeps nothing in this browser.
